output.brief: Pay and the firm-wide hours target do not explain the departures. Salaries sit mid-market like the rest of the firm. The one Brennick & Stowe move was only about £4k higher, not £15k, and most leavers took equal or lower pay. Other groups' attrition is normal, and the target change applied to all groups. Eight of the nine leavers worked on Kestrel, and only 1 of the 13 associates not on it left. So the cause is specific to Kestrel. However, everyone on Kestrel was supervised by Dorian Faulk, and he supervises nothing else. The heavy workload and his supervision therefore can't be told apart from the records. The survey mentions both weekend-heavy work and humiliating late-night corrections. I'm fairly sure about pay and the target, and unsure about supervision versus workload. Don't announce the £12k retention payment or close the review. Commission the confidential outside interviews (about £9k, within three weeks), designed to separate supervision from workload. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition tracking. Hold the supervision change and the £160k contract-reviewer option until the interviews report. Document review runs to the end of December, so the timing is tight but workable.
